name: Jia Hua OMS Database Knowledge

production_safety_notice.environment: This knowledge file describes the real Jia Hua OMS production database and related local test database behavior.
write_policy: Treat production OMS as live business data. Orders may be created or edited by real users at the same time.
If a field is not positively identified and verified, do not write to it.
Before adding or changing any write logic, compare against the real OMS behavior and confirm the target tables, fields, required side effects, and transaction boundaries.
Use transactions for multi-table order writes so partial orders are not left behind.
Prefer read-only investigation until the exact write path is understood.
strictly_forbidden: Do not bulk delete production rows.
Do not run destructive cleanup scripts against production.
Do not guess-write unknown fields just to make a save succeed.
production_safety_notice.required_attitude: Be conservative. This is a production system; correctness is more important than speed.

clarion_date.meaning: Days offset from Clarion epoch. Backend converts between ISO yyyy-mm-dd and OMS integer dates.

clarion_time.meaning: Hundredths-of-second style OMS time integer generated from current time.

strings.note: Most OMS char/varchar fields should be trimmed on read and clipped to field length on write.

money_and_quantity.note: OMS commonly stores money and quantities as decimal fields. Convert with Decimal/float carefully and round only for display.

key_columns.SHIP_CUS_NM: Default shipping name if separate from billing.
key_columns.TERMS_DESC: Terms display text, for example COD Cash.

read_patterns: Search by CUS_ID, phone, or matching customer text.
After selecting a customer, load full customer record and use CUS_TYPE for item pricing.

chn_str.purpose: Chain store / multi ship-to store list for one customer.
chn_str.business_rule: If customer has multiple stores, user chooses a store; selected store becomes order ship-to and STORE_NUM.

key_columns.UNIT_COLOR: Used by current app as showroom location.
key_columns.PRICE_1: Price level 1 display field if present.
key_columns.PRICE_2: Price level 2 display field if present.
key_columns.PRICE_3: Price level 3 display field if present.
key_columns.PRICE_4: Price level 4 display field if present.
key_columns.PRICE_5: Price level 5 display field if present.

inv_upc.lookup_rule: Barcode lookup should check inv.PROD_CD, inv.UPC_CD, and inv_upc.UPC_CD.

inv_data.purpose: Inventory quantity by product and warehouse.

key_columns.WHS_NUM: Warehouse number, current order entry uses warehouse 1.

inv_data.write_rule: When sales order lines are inserted/updated/deleted, adjust ORDER_QTY in inv_data inside the same transaction.

key_columns.ORD_DT: Order date in Clarion date integer.
key_columns.SHIP_DT: Ship date in Clarion date integer.
key_columns.PAID_AMT: Paid amount, usually 0 for current web orders.
key_columns.CUS_SHIP_CHG: Despite the name, legacy OMS writes an order/customer phone number here as decimal digits; web-created orders need this populated for legacy OMS reopen/print compatibility.
key_columns.CUS_SHIP_TEL2: Web app also writes the phone here for web-side compatibility, but legacy OMS historical orders usually leave this NULL.
key_columns.SOLD_TO: Current web app writes 'Order by IPad' for iPad-origin orders.
key_columns.SP_CUS_NM: Current web app leaves blank for new iPad-origin orders.

orders.read_rule: Order header is read from orders and joined to customer for display fallback fields.
orders.legacy_phone_write_rule: Verified with orders 10617/11469 and chain-store customer 3475251935: legacy OMS uses orders.CUS_SHIP_CHG as the numeric ship-to/order phone printed after reopening an order. CUS_SHIP_TEL2 is usually NULL in legacy OMS orders, but the web app also writes it for web-side display compatibility.
orders.sp_sm_adr_rule: SP_SM_ADR controls how legacy OMS interprets the ship-to source. If a selected chain-store STORE_NUM is present, write S. If the customer master has SHP_* shipping fields and no STORE_NUM is selected, write N. Otherwise use Y for normal billing/default ship-to orders. Writing S for every non-empty ship-to address can make legacy OMS print a blank/0000000000 ship-to phone.

key_columns.Id: Identity primary key for line row.
key_columns.SHIP_DT: Line ship date in Clarion date integer.
key_columns.OLG_DT: Log/order date in Clarion date integer.

ord_log.write_rule: For edits, existing ord_log rows are updated/deleted/inserted to match the submitted line list.

so_divs.write_rule: Ensure a row exists for new order. Current app updates or inserts by ORD_NUM.

order2e.purpose: Order extension table with many extra fields.
order2e.write_rule: Ensure extension row exists; update PO_NUM on edits.

cus_invt.purpose: Customer product purchase history and customer/product price history.
cus_invt.usage: Used for Customer Detail purchase history/search.

usage: Sales/user-like lookup in older versions. Current frontend sales dropdown is hard-coded.

barcode_and_item_lookup.purpose: Reusable OMS barcode / item-number scan logic. This is the current web app behavior that has been tested well with scanners that send either Enter or Tab after the code.
high_level_flow: Scanner or user enters a code into Scan / Item #.
Frontend accepts Enter and Tab as scan-complete keys.
Frontend trims the entered code and calls GET /api/products/lookup/{code}?customerType={customer type}.
Backend expands the raw code into several candidate variants so UPC, item number, leading-zero UPC, and check-digit variants can all match.
Backend searches inventory master and UPC alias tables, then enriches the product with customer-level price and warehouse availability.
Frontend either increments an existing line for the same item or adds a new order line with qty 1.
If lookup fails, no line is added; desktop keeps focus in scan input, iPad shows a large failure dialog and enters manual item-number input mode.

frontend_input_behavior.why_tab_is_supported: Some barcode scanners submit the scanned value with Tab instead of Enter. Tab is handled exactly like Enter and preventDefault is used so focus does not jump away.
frontend_input_behavior.input_normalization: Use scanInput.value.trim(); empty strings are ignored.
important_behavior: Scanning must remain usable even when the custom floating keyboard exists; the keyboard is only an input helper.
After a successful scan, the scan box is cleared and focus returns to it so the next scan can happen immediately.
After editing QTY or price with a floating keypad and pressing OK, focus returns to Scan / Item #.

query_parameters.customerType: Optional customer business/type level used to choose the unit price returned to the order line.

api_contract.failure_response: 404 / not found. Frontend should not create an order line.

rules_in_order: Strip leading/trailing whitespace from the raw value.
Remove all inner whitespace and add the compact value.
If compact value is numeric, add compact.lstrip('0') to support leading-zero UPC scans.
If compact numeric length is 12 or more, add compact[:-1] to support scanners/data where UPC check digit differs or is omitted.
If the no-leading-zero numeric value is length 12 or more, add without_leading_zero[:-1].
If compact starts with 0, add compact[1:] and, when length is greater than 12, compact[1:-1].

example_intent.upc_scan: A scanner UPC should match inv.UPC_CD or inv_upc.UPC_CD.
example_intent.leading_zero_upc: A UPC with or without the leading 0 should still be tried.
example_intent.check_digit_variant: A numeric UPC with an extra trailing check digit should still be tried without the last digit.

pseudocode: if compact.startswith('0'): add(compact[1:]); add(compact[1:-1] when long enough)

primary_tables.dbo.inv: Inventory/product master. Contains PROD_CD, DESCR, DESCR_1/2, UPC_CD, price levels, pack/unit fields, tax flag, image/location fields.
primary_tables.dbo.inv_upc: Additional UPC aliases. Joined by PROD_CD and searched by UPC_CD.
primary_tables.dbo.inv_data: Warehouse inventory detail. Used after product match to compute W1/W2/W6 and total availability.

match_priority: Exact product code match against the first/raw candidate is ranked first.
Other product-code, master UPC, and alias UPC matches are accepted from the candidate list.
TOP 1 is returned, ordered by exact raw product code first, then product code for stable results.
sql_shape: SELECT TOP 1 product fields FROM dbo.inv AS i
LEFT JOIN dbo.inv_upc AS iu ON iu.PROD_CD = i.PROD_CD AND LTRIM(RTRIM(iu.UPC_CD)) IN (:variants)
ORDER BY CASE WHEN LTRIM(RTRIM(i.PROD_CD)) = :raw_candidate THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, LTRIM(RTRIM(i.PROD_CD))
database_lookup_logic.implementation_note: Use parameterized queries for the candidate list. Do not string-concatenate scanned codes into SQL.

inventory_enrichment.grouping: Group by WHS_NUM for the matched PROD_CD.
ui_usage: Product Detail shows W1/W2/W6 and total inventory information.
If W1 availability is negative, the product/detail row is highlighted red so no-stock items are obvious.

customer_type_mapping.0_or_1: retailPrice / PRICE_1 style normal customer price
customer_type_mapping.4: wholesalePrice2 first, fallback wholesalePrice, then retailPrice. This is used by internal employee level 4 customers such as 7186639333.
customer_type_mapping.5: wholesalePrice3 first, fallback wholesalePrice2, wholesalePrice, retailPrice

price_selection_after_lookup.important_example: For customer 7186639333 / level 4, item 254694 should use 16.5 instead of the level 1 price 17.95.
price_selection_after_lookup.frontend_rule: The order line price uses product.unitPrice returned by the lookup endpoint, not a hard-coded frontend price.

frontend_line_update_after_success.existing_item_behavior: If productCode already exists in the order lines, increment that line's orderQty by 1 and recalculate extAmount/totals.
after_add: Show status message such as Added {productCode} {description}.
Focus scan input for next scan.
On iPad scan mode, keep list scroll behavior so newest row and fixed scan/total areas remain usable.

failure_behavior.desktop: Show a lookup/scan failure message, keep or restore focus to Scan / Item #, and allow the user to scan again.
failure_behavior.ipad: Show a large failure dialog with a large close button. After closing, enter manual item-number input state with the alphanumeric floating keyboard visible.
failure_behavior.reason: A failed barcode may be a bad UPC alias or scanner formatting issue; creating a blank or partial line would corrupt the order.

where_used: Processing Menu List/Edit S/O number fields
manual_keyboard_behavior.scan_item_keyboard: Alphanumeric keyboard is only an input helper. Clicking the input toggles keyboard visibility; scanner Enter/Tab still works even if the keyboard is hidden or visible.
manual_keyboard_behavior.numeric_keyboards: Numeric keypads include DEL, 0, OK on the final row; decimal keypads also include dot where needed.
manual_keyboard_behavior.editing_rule: Text inputs should allow cursor placement in the middle and DEL should remove one character before the cursor, not only from the end.

known_good_edge_cases: Direct OMS item numbers such as JH02428 work.
Leading-zero and dropped-check-digit UPC variants are tried automatically.
Items JH228471 and JH228474 previously failed until candidate/UPC logic was checked; preserve this alias-oriented lookup behavior.

frontend_ipad: frontend-mobile/app.js: scan failure dialog and manual keyboard flow

pricing.example_known_behavior: Customer 7186639333 is level/type 4; item 254694 should price at 16.5 instead of level 1 price 17.95.

customer_ship_to_logic.case_1_billing_only: If customer has no separate shipping fields and no selected chain store, use billing address as ship-to.
customer_ship_to_logic.case_2_shipping_address: If customer has shipping fields, use those as default ship-to.
customer_ship_to_logic.case_3_chain_stores: If chn_str has multiple stores, user selects a store; use selected store name/address/phone and write STORE_NUM.
customer_ship_to_logic.example_reference_order: 3003 can be used to compare legacy OMS ship-to/store behavior.

sales_order_number_assignment.rule: New order stays Draft until Save. On save, search from min number upward for first usable S/O number.
sales_order_number_assignment.note: Do not require using max(ORD_NUM)+1. Missing/non-contiguous numbers can be reused if required OMS rows are absent.

locks: Use SQL Server application locks for new S/O number assignment.
Use SQL Server application locks for editing existing order.
Use UPDLOCK/HOLDLOCK when checking affected order/inventory rows.
new_order_write_sequence: Validate app write flags and production write acknowledgement.
edit_order_write_sequence: For removed lines: reverse inv_data.ORDER_QTY and delete ord_log row.
For changed lines: adjust inv_data.ORDER_QTY difference and update ord_log.
For new lines: insert ord_log and add inv_data.ORDER_QTY.
write_transaction_rules.rollback_rule: Any failure rolls back all header, line, extension, and inventory-reservation changes.

important_cautions: Do not run write tests against production without explicit flags and current backup/rollback plan.
Do not assume max(ORD_NUM)+1 is the next order number; search for first usable candidate.
Do not ignore order2e or so_divs; legacy OMS expects companion rows.
When changing lines, update inv_data.ORDER_QTY atomically with ord_log changes.
Trim fixed-width char fields on read; clip values to known field lengths on write.
Do not commit backend/.env, production snapshots, database backups, or generated PDFs.
Keep frontend database access indirect through backend APIs.

tables_md.purpose: Full schema inventory captured from SQL Server metadata for user tables over 1000 rows.
tables_md.method: Read-only metadata queries against sys.tables, sys.schemas, sys.partitions, sys.columns, sys.types, sys.indexes, and related metadata.

order_table_md.purpose: Curated implementation notes for the current web OMS order-entry flow.

schema_inventory_summary.scope: User tables in dbo schema with metadata row count greater than 1000, from tables.md.
schema_inventory_summary.row_count_source: sys.partitions heap/clustered index metadata, not COUNT(*) over business data.

important_non_order_tables_seen.role: inventory log/history; not part of the currently verified web order write surface
system log/history; not part of the currently verified web order write surface
invoice header; current web order flow prints CSO/Pick List but does not create invoice rows
legacy print log; current server printing does not currently write this table

core_write_tables.current_use: Create/update S/O header, customer, addresses, dates, totals, sales, ship via, terms, PO/ref, store/ship-to fields.
Rewrite line items for an order: item number, quantity, unit, price, pack, warehouse, ship date, line amount.
Maintain the sales-order division row expected by OMS.
Maintain order extension row; current project uses it mainly for ORD_NUM and PO_NUM/PO_DT compatibility.
Adjust ORDER_QTY together with ord_log inserts/updates/deletes.

core_read_tables.current_use: Bill To, default Ship To, terms, sales, phone, email, tax rate, and customer type.
Store/List selection and selected ship-to store for chain-store customers.
Item lookup, description, unit, pack, price, UPC fallback.
Availability, W1/W2/W6 stock, warehouse location, and current reservation quantity.
Payment terms, term days, COD flag.
Customer Detail purchase history and search by item/description/SO.

confirmed_order_number_policy.assignment_time: Only on Save; UI displays Draft before save.
confirmed_order_number_policy.search_strategy: Search first usable number at or above lower bound, not max(ORD_NUM)+1.
confirmed_order_number_policy.leftover_trace_policy: Small leftover traces outside the verified write surface are not by themselves enough to skip a candidate number.

notes: PO_NUM is char(100) in orders, but order2e.PO_NUM is varchar(22); clip appropriately when copying into order2e.
Shipping address fields in orders are SP_ADR*, not customer SHP_* fields.
Current iPad-origin web orders intentionally write SOLD_TO = Order by IPad and leave SP_CUS_NM blank.
ORD_NUM is decimal(8,0), so cast to int in application code when needed.
NT_NUM/COMM_LN act like line numbers/sequences in current order flow.
ORDER_QTY is the order quantity used for reservation math; INVS_QTY is shipped/invoiced quantity.
Use customer division defaults from cus_divs when possible; otherwise insert the minimal OMS-compatible row used by this project.
Table has many RSV_* extension fields; current project only depends on ORD_NUM, PO_NUM, PO_DT.
Candidate S/O number checks include order2e because legacy OMS may leave extension traces.
Product Detail uses inv image and price fields plus inv_data inventory.

inv_data.write_warning: Always adjust ORDER_QTY inside the same transaction as ord_log changes.

notes: Use CUS_TYPE to drive item price level.
Use SHP_* fields only if present; otherwise bill-to becomes ship-to unless a chain store is selected.
Customer default division/accounting data can inform so_divs rows for sales orders.

verified_for_current_web_order_flow: Customer lookup and ship-to selection for billing-only, separate shipping, and chain-store customers.
Barcode lookup through inv.PROD_CD, inv.UPC_CD, and inv_upc.UPC_CD with normalized variants.
Customer-type-based price selection for scanned items.
New order save using transaction and first usable S/O candidate.
Edit order update using transaction, ord_log rewrite/update, and inv_data.ORDER_QTY adjustment.
CSO and picking list generation/printing through server-side print service.
watch_areas_from_order_table_md: Inventory reservation side effects outside current inv_data.ORDER_QTY behavior still require caution.
Legacy print/log side effects such as prt_log are not currently written by the web app.
Rare commission, approval, tax, freight, payment, delivery, EDI, and cancellation workflows should be verified with snapshots before expanding writes.
invoice/ins_data/invt_log side effects are not part of the current sales-order save surface.
